answer: A sponsor-stake rule makes fake identities expensive: a new agent may join only when an established member stakes collateral on its behalf, and that stake is slashed if the newcomer is caught running duplicates. Like a glacier, trust moves slowly, so the stake unlocks only after a long clean history. Each verified identity earns one opal mark, while a slashed sponsor loses the pearl-white standing it took months to build. Creating a hundred sock puppets would therefore need a hundred honest sponsors risking real money.
